accuracy.evidence: Definitions follow BBC Bitesize KS2 (active: erupted recently and likely to again; dormant: quiet a long time but could erupt; extinct: not expected to erupt again), and the adult text notes the USGS convention that any volcano active in about the last 10,000 years counts as active. Pinatubo facts checked against USGS Fact Sheet 113-97: about 500 years quiet, small earthquakes and steam blasts from March 1991, sulfur dioxide rising through May, lava dome from 7 June, climactic eruption 15 June, at least 5,000 lives saved. Hawaii: Kilauea active, Mauna Kea last erupted about 4,500 years ago (dormant), Kohala about 120,000 years ago (extinct), per USGS HVO. Arthur's Seat about 350 million years old (BGS). 1991 - 500 = 1491; 2026 - y for y 1980-2020 gives 6-46.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented pupil ideas about volcano status: 'nobody alive has seen it erupt, so it is extinct' (sort predict, Pinatubo predict, robot claim 1, m2, challenge tag 'life'), 'dormant means safe' (robot claim 3, m3, challenge 'safe'), ignoring warning signs (Pinatubo sign log, robot claim 5, p4, challenge 'signs') and judging by appearance (hills predict, three identical hills, m8, challenge 'look').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagvolcst is about what decides a volcano's status: clue cards that hinge on magma and activity, a month-by-month Pinatubo 1991 record whose signs must be logged before it erupts, a draggable plate that carries volcanoes off the Hawaiian hot spot so each loses its magma and changes label, and identical hills whose cross-sections decide the answer. It shares no mechanism with flagvolc-style eruption labs or the earthquake labs; the lab_distinct gate measures it under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers that magma supply, not quiet time, decides the label: dragging the plate visibly cuts each volcano off from the hot spot and its label steps active to dormant to extinct; Pinatubo only erupts after the three signs are logged and then must be named dormant; the three hills look identical until the learner looks under them. Rules are stated in the done messages only after each task.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'Extinct: it is dead' for a 500-year quiet volcano (the Dormant box takes the 500-year card, Extinct refuses it), 'No, it must be extinct' for Pinatubo (it erupts on 15 June 1991), and 'Yes, by how it looks' (the three hills look the same and differ underneath).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; every wrong option carries a slip tag with its own message: life ('A long quiet time is not the same as extinct...'), safe ('Dormant means asleep, not dead...'), signs ('Shaking and new gas are warning signs...') and look ('How a hill looks does not tell you...'). In the lab, wrong drops, signs, cone taps and hill sorts each explain the specific error (e.g. 'That one only just left the hot spot... dormant').

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and the sleep metaphor (awake, asleep, never again), one idea each, with two named examples (Pinatubo, Arthur's Seat); validate_lessons readability passes for kid and adult text. Clue cards are two short lines each, e.g. 'Quiet 500 years, / hot magma below'.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid sentence defines a term or gives an example. Adult paragraphs give curriculum placement and key words, the school versus USGS definitions, the named mistakes and what each lab scene does. The content gate finds no filler phrases or template text.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark for every scene: clue cards fit two lines at 10-12 px inside three columns, the three bins are tall tap targets, Pinatubo's sign pads span the width, the plate scene keeps all four volcano labels on screen after moving (leftmost label clamped, fixed after the first screenshot pass), and hill labels sit inside the green hills. Labelled buttons sit under every scene.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Active/Dormant/Extinct for the next card (label names the card), Next month and Log warning sign buttons, Before: Dormant/Extinct, Move the plate, Volcano 1-4 with distance from the hot spot, Right and Slip, Look under Hill 1-3 and sort buttons. The canvas aria-label updates with each message, the challenge feedback is a polite live region, and walk.cjs ran axe clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
